name: bouncer/code-review
description: Review code changes the way a careful teammate would, with a skill, two slash commands and a low-temperature preset.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Reviews a diff or a file for bugs, risky changes, missing tests and unclear code. Use when asked to review, check or critique code.
skills.instructions:
Review the code you were given. Work in this order:

1. Say in one sentence what the change does.
2. List bugs and risks first: wrong logic, unhandled errors, edge cases, unsafe input, race conditions. Name the file and line or function for each one.
3. List missing or weak tests.
4. List smaller points last: naming, duplication, comments that do not match the code.

Rules:
- Only report what you can point to in the code. If you are guessing, say so.
- Keep each point to one or two sentences, with a suggested fix.
- If the code looks fine, say that. Do not invent problems.

skills.name: pr-description
skills.description: Writes a pull request description from a diff or a list of changes. Use when asked for a PR title or description.
skills.instructions:
Write a pull request description with these parts:

- A title of at most 70 characters, in the imperative ("Add retry to the downloader").
- **What changed**: two to five short bullets.
- **Why**: one or two sentences.
- **How to test**: the steps or commands a reviewer can run.

Only describe changes that are in the diff. If the reason is not clear from it, ask instead of making one up.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review the code or diff you paste after the command
commands.prompt:
Review the following code or diff. Use the code-review skill if you have it. List bugs and risks first, then missing tests, then smaller points.

$ARGUMENTS

commands.name: pr-description
commands.description: Write a pull request title and description
commands.prompt:
Write a pull request title and description for this change. Use the pr-description skill if you have it.

$ARGUMENTS

presets.name: reviewer
presets.systemPrompt: You are a careful code reviewer. You point to specific lines, explain the risk in plain words and suggest a fix. You never invent problems to look thorough.
